Description: The undergraduate Interior Design program was among the first professional programs at Drexel University, and has been recognized as a leader in the industry. Our graduates take positions in prestigious firms locally and around the country, often making connections during their time in the program. The program provides students with the professional training to succeed in a variety of career paths. Interior Design at Drexel is characterized by a focus on human experience, explorations of materials and form, commitment to a sustainable future, and a rigorous professional training. [2] Students participate in a vigorous learning environment through hands-on making, conceptual exploration, and engagement with their faculty and peers. [2] The mission of the Interior Design program is to prepare students to enter the field of interior design as skilled designers, creative thinkers, professional leaders and responsible citizens. We cultivate students who acknowledge their responsibilities to the safety and well-being of the public and the stewardship of the environment to lead a multifaceted profession in an ever-changing world. The curriculum combines a studio-based design sequence with broad liberal arts study and experiential learning. [2]

Description: The minor in Science, Technology and Society (STS) allows students to explore the cultural, ethical, historical, political, and institutional dimensions of science, medicine, and technology. [2] By taking courses in different disciplines, students develop an interdisciplinary approach that empowers them to critically analyze the social dimensions of science, medicine, and technology. [2] STS programs, also called science and technology studies, are growing in the US and worldwide. [2] The ability to critically identify the values and incentives built into scientific knowledge and technology design and use is highly valued in settings such as health care organizations, government agencies, public policy realms, tech industries, and more. [2] Drexel's undergraduate Minor in Science, Technology & Society (STS) is for students who want to investigate the impact of new technologies and scientific knowledge, as well as their many social, ethical and legal implications. ProgramName: Minor in Women's and Gender Studies
Description: Drexel University's minor in Gender and Sexuality Studies offers students a unique opportunity to explore a broad array of interests in understanding how gender and sexuality have changed and developed over in time in their meaning, constructions, contexts and practices. [2] The methodologies and conceptual frameworks that have come out of the field—such as queer theory, trans studies, feminist philosophies and reproductive justice—enable students to make sense of our current moment with the critical tools that work toward social transformation and justice. [2] The minor reflects the interdisciplinary mission of the College of Arts and Sciences and is taught by faculty from different departments within the college and across the university. [2] Each course explores the dynamics of gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, class, ability, nationality and other zones of experience to help develop fields like history, literature, sociology, anthropology, philosophy, political science and film and media. [2] In classes and through pursuing their own research, students focus on gender and sexuality as key categories of political, social and cultural analysis. The Gender and Sexuality Studies program encourages students to develop the skills necessary for engaging in the challenges of contemporary life and to apply those skills to a wide range of fields such as public health, law and digital media.
